questions.question: Distinguish between using goods efficiently and using them effectively, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Efficient: getting the most use from a resource with the least waste, e.g. switching off lights, fixing leaks. Effective: using a resource so that it achieves its purpose, e.g. using a calculator correctly in a maths test; studying the right chapter.

questions.question: Explain reduce, reuse and recycle, and why reduce comes first.
questions.expected_answer: Reduce: use and buy less, e.g. own shopping bag, less packaging. Reuse: use an item again, e.g. glass jars for storage, passing on uniforms. Recycle: process used materials into new products, e.g. cans, paper, plastic bottles. Reduce comes first because it avoids using resources at all; recycling still uses energy, transport and materials.

questions.question: Give two ways in which recycling benefits the economy and the environment.
questions.expected_answer: Economy (any): creates income for waste pickers and buy-back centres; jobs in recycling factories; small upcycling businesses; saves municipalities landfill costs. Environment (any): conserves natural resources; reduces litter and pollution; saves energy; extends landfill life.
